text:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 streaming latency breach detected for /v1/streaming.generate in region us-west-2. p99=2.8s (SLO=1.2s), p95=540ms. Severity=P1. Paging @oncall-sre.

samir-k: I see sudden tail starting 20:13:42 UTC, coincides with spike in long-sequence sessions. Clients reporting stalled chunks and long gaps between tokens.

leah-w: No code deploys in last 2 hrs. Infra metrics: GPU temperature climbing on a subset of hosts in placement-group pg-west-2a.

tom-h: pulling node telemetry now. `rictl list-hosts --pool streaming-west | grep thermal` shows gpu-node-88 and gpu-node-91 with thermal=85C and ECC_correctable_count high on 91.

priya-g: CS message: 5 customers affected, 2 enterprise flagged. One enterprise reports continuous reconnects. Mark customer-impact=true.

oncall-sre: acknowledged. Triage plan: 1) identify nodes with worst metrics, 2) quick live mitigations (drain, spillover, fallback), 3) notify customers and exec comms, 4) collect artifacts.

samir-k: digging into traces: streaming stalls originate during KV cache miss-heavy paths when seq_len > 5k. When GPU enters throttle, page-ins from host memory take longer and attention op waits.

infra-bot: hardware-alert: gpu-node-91: ECC_correctable=720 in last 15min, thermal=86C, fan=2200rpm.

leah-w: recommend immediate targeted exclusion of 88/91 and reroute traffic. Also consider enabling CPU fallback for public traffic.

tom-h: command ready: ```rictl node exclude --node gpu-node-91 --reason "thermal+ecc" --until 2660000000``` and ```rictl routing spillover --pool streaming-west --to pool=streaming-east --max-rr 0.25```

oncall-sre: hold on spillover — check capacity east. If we spill too fast, we might overload remote pools. Samir, can we do a gradual spillover and FIFO drain?

samir-k: yes. Plan: 1) exclude nodes 88 & 91 from new allocations; 2) start graceful connection drain on those nodes; 3) start 15% spillover to streaming-east, monitor p99; 4) enable model fallback q4_int8 for non-enterprise tag.

priya-g: enterprise customers must stay on GPU; we should fail over their sessions only to healthy GPU nodes in other AZs, not CPU fallback. I'll coordinate CS.

oncall-sre: executing excludes and drain now.

incident-bot: Action: node exclusion and drain started by oncall-sre at 20:17:03 UTC.

infra-bot: scale-event: requested +4 a100-small preemptible to streaming-west; provisioning started.

samir-k: after exclusion, p99 improved from 2.8s -> 1.1s in ~3 minutes. p95 stable ~420ms. Streaming stall errors dropped ~70%.

leah-w: ECC counters on 91 continue to increment even as traffic drops — suggests hardware instability rather than load-induced transient. Recommend decommission after incident.

tom-h: grabbing nvidia-smi dump and kernel logs. Snippet: ```Dec 01 20:12:45 kernel: NVRM: GPU 0000:3b:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.```. That's not great.

priya-g: CS update: enterprise customer A experienced a 10-minute session interruption; we've offered remediation and are preparing an incident email.

oncall-sre: propose mitigation window: keep non-enterprise fallback for 60 minutes, keep excluded nodes offline for at least 30m then mark for replacement. If p99 <1.3s for 30m, we downgrade severity.

samir-k: suggested follow-ups: - add auto-exclude rule when ECC_correctable_rate > 150/min for a node - backpressure at KV cache layer when memmap latency > 200ms - sticky failover for enterprise sessions across GPU pools

leah-w: I'll open infra ticket INF-9021 to replace gpu-node-91 and run diagnostics on 88. Also note to run extended burn-in on replacement host.

tom-h: attaching diagnostics commands for postmortem: ```# ECC counters
rictl node-ecc --node gpu-node-91 --json > ecc-91.log
# thermal timeline
rictl node-thermal --node gpu-node-91 --since 30m > thermal-91.log
# nvidia-smi
ssh gpu-node-91 "nvidia-smi -q -x > /tmp/nv-91.xml"```

incident-bot: Mitigation summary logged: excluded 88/91, started graceful drain, scaled +4 a100-small, enabled fallback for non-enterprise.

priya-g: CS will send interim notification to impacted customers within 30 minutes. Keeping execs updated.

oncall-sre: monitoring p99 every 2m. Current p99=1.08s. If stable for 30m, downgrade to P2 and close on-call.

samir-k: collecting traces and will run a synthetic long-seq streaming eval to ensure latency stable. Also snapshot KV miss patterns pre/post mitigation.

leah-w: action items for postmortem: hardware replacement timeline, auto-exclude config, KV cache pressure defense, and enterprise sticky failover policy.

priya-g: volunteer postmortem lead: me for customer comms. Samir will lead technical RCA. Leah will coordinate infra replacement.

incident-bot: Next automated check-in at 20:27 UTC. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
